missionPremise: The row's premise (P-276, OPS-24): src/lib/secret-rotation.mjs rotates ROTATION_TARGETS, a frozen two-key object (neondb, hauska_mcp) whose descriptors carry NO project, into ONE project resolved from the environment (GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT, default hauska-prod-497015), while LDT's staging connection secret lives in a different project (legacy-design-tools-prod) and was repointed by hand on 2026-09-16 (A-181, version 6). A copy of the same connection string in the other project is therefore never written by the rotation, and if its value can differ from the rotated one it can strand a consumer on a dead endpoint. Source: _dispatches/2026-09-17_p276-staging-secret-targets_dispatch.md, 'The row's premise, and a measurement that challenges it'.
completionPredicate: Every staging connection secret that a Cloud Run resource actually consumes in BOTH projects (hauska-prod-497015, legacy-design-tools-prod) is either (a) a rotation target in the rotation project, or (b) byte-identical to one -- and that disjunction is enforced by something that FAILS when it stops holding, reads its consumer list from the services' own configuration rather than from memory, and refuses (never passes) when a value is unreadable or a project unlistable. The consumer list travels with its counting rule and its timestamp.
scopeBasis: Boundaries and why: (1) the work is READ-ONLY against GCP -- the dispatch forbids running staging-reset, rotating or writing any secret, or deploying, so the control was built and then exercised with reads (gcloud secrets versions access + run services/jobs list) and env-only overrides; (2) src/jobs/verify-walk.mjs (P-301) and the rail writers (P-266/P-268) are untouched by the diff (verified by `git diff --name-status HEAD^..HEAD`); (3) the third rotation target the row asks for was deliberately NOT added, on measured IAM grounds stated below; (4) the clone is a fresh origin/main clone under P:/tmp per the dispatch, not a property worktree.

canItChange.answer: YES, the written value CAN differ from the previous one -- but only on three conditions, none of which occurred on 2026-09-17, and the measured six resets produced byte-identical values. The stable-branch restore path rewrites the SAME branch id and endpoint, so on that path the URI is a pure function of unchanged inputs; a differing value requires (a) the CREATE path, (b) an endpoint re-home, or (c) an out-of-band role-password change.
canItChange.valueWritten: src/lib/secret-rotation.mjs:85 fetchNeonConnectionUri() -> GET /projects/{projectId}/connection_uri?branch_id=..&database_name=..&role_name=..&pooled=false (:87), with refusePoolerHost() (:90). Inputs: projectId (the Neon project, from staging-reset's *_NEON_PROJECT_ID), branchId, databaseName, roleName, and Neon's current password for roleName.

The host is READ BACK at :179 via branchDirectHost (:135-150), never assumed -- the file's own comment (:112-115) says a restore that silently re-homed the endpoint would reintroduce the defect the stable branch replaces.

An out-of-band role-password rotation, with no branch reset, would change the URI on the restore path too. Nothing in this repo rotates that password; it is the residual way a value can move between resets.

designDecisions.decision: The consumer list is read from the RESOURCES' OWN CONFIGURATION -- every env valueFrom.secretKeyRef of every Cloud Run service and job in both projects, read by field -- with two helpers because the JSON paths differ (services: spec.template.spec.containers; jobs: spec.template.spec.template.spec.containers), plus a filter that keeps only STAGING_* names.
designDecisions.why: The dispatch requires it ('not from memory'), and the difference is measurable: the earlier enumeration in this lane read 49 resources / 9 consumer bindings and today's run reads 50 / 10, the delta being factory-republish-on-change, which P-294 merged and deployed between the two reads. A remembered list would have been silently stale the same day it was written.
designDecisions.alternativeRejected: A checked-in list of consumers. Rejected: it goes stale on the next job deploy and cannot distinguish 'no consumer' from 'not looked'.

designDecisions.decision: Four verdicts per consumed (project, secret) pair -- rotation-target (a target exists at that project+name), identical-to-target (latest-value sha256 equals a rotation target's latest-value sha256), drift (readable but matches neither), unmeasured (its value could not be read) -- and ok is false when there is ANY drift or ANY unmeasured. An unlistable project is PROJECT_UNREACHABLE/refusal, never a pass.
designDecisions.why: The row's disjunction is 'a target OR provably identical to one'; anything else must fail, and a value that cannot be read must not be indistinguishable from a value that agrees. The unit tests cover all four verdicts and the test file asserts the negative direction for each.
designDecisions.whatItCosts: An unreadable secret makes the check red rather than quiet. That is deliberate (silent fallbacks are the defect class the program hunts) and it is why --projects exists: the reset job's identity reaches hauska-prod-497015 but not legacy-design-tools-prod, so a one-project caller must not read its own coverage as two-project coverage.

designDecisions.decision: A single place resolves the rotation project (rotationProject, src/lib/secret-rotation.mjs:65-67: GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT || GCP_PROJECT || 'hauska-prod-497015') and a single place lists the targets with their projects (rotationTargetList, :75-83, derived from ROTATION_TARGETS itself), and rotateSecret now takes a per-target projectId override (:99). The dry run and the drift control both consume rotationTargetList, never a second copy.
designDecisions.why: The drift control's notion of 'a rotation target' must be the rotation's own notion, or the control can pass while the writer disagrees with it. One fact, one place: adding a target above makes it appear in the listing with no second edit, which the test asserts by comparing the dry run's keys to Object.keys(ROTATION_TARGETS).

designDecisions.decision: The third rotation target the row asks for was NOT added. LDT's STAGING_ATOMS_DATABASE_URL is not turned on; instead the descriptor and the grant it needs are recorded in src/lib/secret-rotation.mjs:39-52 (the gated `atoms` line: {dbName hauska_mcp, roleName neondb_owner, secretName STAGING_ATOMS_DATABASE_URL, secretProjectId legacy-design-tools-prod, storeKey hauska_mcp}).
designDecisions.why: Measured, not argued: (a) the factory-staging-reset job runs as 172690833726-compute@developer.gserviceaccount.com (gcloud run jobs describe, field spec.template.spec.template.spec.serviceAccountName); (b) that identity is in NO binding of legacy-design-tools-prod's project IAM policy (gcloud projects get-iam-policy: members are 1062716564162-* , gha-deployer@legacy-design-tools-prod, api-server-runtime@legacy-design-tools-prod, service-* agents, user:empressaioemail@gmail.com); (c) STAGING_ATOMS_DATABASE_URL's secret-level IAM grants secretAccessor to api-server-runtime@legacy-design-tools-prod ONLY (gcloud secrets get-iam-policy). Adding the target would therefore fail closed with PERMISSION_DENIED on every reset and break the publish path it exists to protect -- and a cross-project secret write is one of OPS-24's three operator stop points ('a new credential or secret mount').
designDecisions.alternativeRejected: Adding the target and letting it fail closed until the grant lands. Rejected: an always-failing write in the reset job is worse than a recorded, gated descriptor, and the row's disjunction is held by the drift control instead.
designDecisions.reversal: One IAM binding (secretAccessor for the factory job identity on that secret, plus whatever the write path needs) turns the descriptor on with a one-line edit; the storeKey indirection the descriptor needs is already implemented and tested (secret-rotation.mjs:120-122).

designDecisions.decision: Where the check runs, stated with what each venue can reach: NOT in CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml` has no credentials step and no `secrets.` reference at all -- read at source -- so a GitHub runner cannot list Cloud Run or read Secret Manager), and NOT from inside factory-staging-reset (that image's final stage is `node:22-slim` with only `npm install --omit=dev`, i.e. no gcloud CLI -- read at source -- and its identity reaches only hauska-prod-497015). It runs ON DEMAND / as a scheduled job under an identity holding roles/run.viewer + roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor in BOTH projects, which is what this lane used from the operator host.
designDecisions.why: A control whose execution venue quietly cannot reach half its scope would report 'no drift' for the unreachable half. Naming the venue and its reach is part of the control's contract; --projects exists so a caller can be honest about partial coverage.

falsifiersPreRegistered.falsifier: A consumed staging secret missing from the targets, and not identical to one, fails the check (test).
falsifiersPreRegistered.registeredAnswer: It fails, in three independent ways: (1) offline unit tests with crafted consumers (a drift case, an identical-copy case, a same-name-different-project case in BOTH directions, and an unmeasured case); (2) the script's own --selftest, which runs those four cases and refuses to report ok unless it observed both directions; (3) a LIVE negative control -- the check re-run against the real projects with the rotation project overridden to legacy-design-tools-prod (env only, no writes), which returns ok:false, exit 4, and grades both real consumed secrets 'drift' because they are no longer targets and match no readable target hash. Evidence: CP2.

falsifiersPreRegistered.registeredAnswer: It lists both targets with project hauska-prod-497015 and mode dry-run / writes 0, derived from ROTATION_TARGETS; a unit test asserts the listed keys EQUAL Object.keys(ROTATION_TARGETS) and that the listed project is the project the writer actually resolves, so a target added to the object and not the listing (or the reverse) fails the test.
